newsitem.title: USA: Texaco former executive's hearing postponed.
newsitem.headline: Texaco former executive's hearing postponed.

text.p: A U.S. federal magistrate on Tuesday postponed a preliminary hearing for 30 days in the case against a former Texaco Inc executive accused of planning to destroy documents in a racial discrimination lawsuit.

The preliminary hearing, which was scheduled for Wednesday, is now slated for February 13, unless a plea deal can be reached in the case against Richard Lundwall, a former senior coordinator for personnel services in Texaco's finance department.
Last month, federal prosecutors sought a first extension to provide time for plea negotiations.
The U.S. attorney's office in Manhattan said it did not file any additional papers in the latest postponement.
Lundwall, who was forced into retirement in August as part of staff reductions, is among those who have been punished by Texaco for their role in the alleged scheme.
The incident came to light after Lundwall turned over secret tapes he had made of himself and other Texaco officials discussing the destruction of papers requested in the discrimination suit.
